When two conclusions appear to agree, their cosine similarity is computed; if above a learned threshold, they are merged into a single node with the averaged embedding.", "scope": {"covers": ["systems with a learned semantic representation of claims"], "excludes": ["purely symbolic systems without embeddings"]}, "forbidden": [{"case": "Two claims with high cosine similarity are merged, but they have different truth conditions in a counterfactual scenario that the embedding fails to capture because it was trained only on observed data.", "eval": "program:embedding_counterfactual_divergence"}, {"case": "Two claims with low cosine similarity are kept separate, but they are logically equivalent and the embedding failed to learn the equivalence due to sparse training data.", "eval": "program:embedding_missed_equivalence"}], "prose_notes": "This criterion risks both over-merging when embeddings are too coarse and under-merging when embeddings are too fine, depending on training data and model capacity."}
